items.claim: `paintWithColor`/`solid` multiply a non-hex color's alpha into `opacity`
`strokeHasInk`/`strokeKey` report ink for a non-finite dash
`lerpPaint` turns a conic angle the long way round
`sampleResolvedStops` returns the earlier coincident stop at the shared offset
items.note: At exactly the first offset, coincident first stops also take the later one now. The property test's "past either end" check no longer samples exactly at the first offset.

This needed a behavior call. When both sides have arrays of the same length they interpolate entry by entry, and a missing width entry reads as that stroke's own width. When the lengths differ, the nearer side's array is kept. I recorded the call in `docs/unruled.md` and removed the matching Open line.

items.claim: `lerpPaint` turns a fully transparent solid black
items.note: `mixColor` now keeps the color when both sides are clear, the way `mixStopColor` already did, and `mixStopColor` now just calls it.
`colorLiteralToCss` now writes those spaces as hex, and its test was updated to match.

items.claim: `parsesAsColor` fallback accepts multi-value strings that start with a color function
items.note: The check now balances parentheses, so nested functions like `color-mix(…, rgb(…))` still pass.

items.claim: paintPreviewCss places a non-`bounds` radial or conic gradient's center at its raw coordinate as a percentage, so the chip shows almost no ramp
colorLiteralToHex refuses an `hsl` literal the palette's own type documents and the package can convert
oklchDegToHex returns gray when asked for far more chroma than exists, the use its doc advertises
parsesAsColor's fallback refuses most of the CSS named colors parseColor reads
lerpPaint, lerpFill and lerpStroke throw on a solid or stop color parseColor cannot read
paletteColorAt and GHOST_STROKE_COLOR answer `#rrggbb` where the module promises `#rrggbbaa`
paletteColorAt reads a fractional `seq` as a missing entry and returns the fallback
solid / paintWithColor move only a *hex* alpha to opacity, so a functional color's alpha multiplies with the kept opacity
